(the “Company”) identified errors in its historical accounting for labor and overhead included in inventories. The historical process allocated certain labor and overhead between raw materials, work in process and finished goods using budget-based percentages and allocation bases that were not sufficiently supported. The process also did not consistently limit capitalized costs to eligible acquisition and production costs, allocate variable overhead based on actual activity, allocate fixed overhead based on normal capacity, or adjust standard or budgeted amounts so that they approximated actual cost. The Company concluded that the historical process did not comply with the inventory-costing requirements in ASC 330, Inventory. As a result, inventories were overstated and cost of revenue were misstated. 1620749.excerpt: Item 4.02 Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements or a Related Audit Report or Interim Review On October 26, 2026 the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors (the "Audit Committee") of Panamera Holdings Corporation (the "Company"), after discussion with management, concluded that the Company's previously issued audited consolidated financial statements as of and for the fiscal years ended July 31, 2025, 2024, 2023 and 2022, included in the Company's Annual Reports on Form 10-K filed on January 6, 2023 (as amended on September 19, 2023), November 16, 2023, January 13, 2025 and November 25, 2025, and the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for the quarterly periods ended April 30, 2022 through April 30, 2026, included in the Company's Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q (together, the "Non-Reliance Periods") should no longer be relied upon. Related earnings releases, reports and communications describing those financial statements should also no longer be relied upon. The conclusion resulted from the Company's determination that it did not record or disclose its obligations under an employment agreement dated February 18, 2022 between the Company and a former Vice President (the "Employment Agreement"). The Employment Agreement, signed on behalf of the Company by its then Chairman, provided for an annual base salary of $250,000 for a three-year term. The Company made no salary payments under it.
